definition: The informal premium charged by the Gray Zone-level vendors, cooks, or service workers to Tier 3+ clients who venture down to purchase authentic low-tier goods or experiences. Part resentment, part necessity — the extra Φ rarely gets reported.
origin: the Gray Zone street economics, coined by market vendors in Old Harbor's lower transit corridors
usage: the Gray Zone vendors, Tier 3 tourists, savvy mid-tier buyers who know to negotiate
example: He thought he was getting authentic the Gray Zone noodles at a deal, but Mama Seo hit him with the flavor tax and he still walked away smiling.
